title: FastPath mini-roll: ops protocol + field notes (May 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an operational protocol for the "fastpath" mini-roll experiment (May 2026). The goal is a low-risk, small-batch progressive rollout that validates new scheduling heuristics and a KV-cache priming optimization in production traffic. This is intentionally narrow: small percent of traffic, short windows, tight rollback criteria. Field notes capture decisions and anomalies during the run for post-mortem and tuning.

Scope & constraints:
- Target surface: hosted API inference lane (production region us-west-2) only. No dedicated/private customers in scope.
- Models impacted: model-v2.3 (primary) with model-v2.2 as fallback. Quantization/INT8 profile unchanged.
- Traffic slice: 1% new-fastpath route joined into routing table; max burstable to 3% for 15m if metrics stable.
- Duration: planned 4-hour window (can be extended to 8h by run lead).

TL;DR rollout plan:
1) Preflight (T-24h to T-1h): config checks, synthetic warmups, baseline metrics snapshot.
2) T0: enable route for 0.1% traffic. Observe 10 minute verification window.
3) T0+10m: if green, move to 0.5%. Observe 20m.
4) T0+30m: move to 1.0%. Observe 30m.
5) T0+1h: optional burst to 3% for 15m for capacity checking.
6) T0+1h20m: if stable, leave at 1% for remainder of window and begin post-run checks.

Roles & critical contacts:
- Run lead: Priya Nair (pager backup: Ravi Patel)
- Serving runtime owner: Ethan Brooks
- SRE & infra: Marta Silva (oncall: marta-sre)
- Product PM: Jia Li
- Customer incident liaison: Sam Ortega
- Slack primary channel: #release-fastpath
- Pager rotation: eng-oncall (see internal rota).

Preflight checklist (T-24h, T-2h, T-30m):
- [ ] Confirm traffic tag and route config reviewed in routing-config PR (see linked PR).
- [ ] Deployment artifact built and SHA pinned: runtime:v2.3.4-fastpath (verify checksum).
- [ ] Canary infra health: node CPU < 60%, GPU memory headroom >= 20% across target pool.
- [ ] KV cache priming script validated on staging; synthetic prefix distribution match > 0.9 correlation.
- [ ] Observability dashboards up: latency p50/p95/p99, error rate (4xx/5xx), token/sec, cost-per-token estimate, tail kernel time.
- [ ] Alerts configured and muted appropriately for expected noise (documented in alert-silence).
- [ ] Smoke test plan loaded into runbook and test harness available: smoke-suite-fastpath.sh.
- [ ] Rollback runbook verified and contact list confirmed.

Rollout calendar (compact timeline):
- 09:00 PT T-24h: Final readiness meeting (15m) — stakeholders: run lead, SRE, runtime.
- 20:00 PT T-2h: Run lead confirm go/no-go on Slack + record baseline metrics snapshot.
- 08:30 PT T-1h: Synthetic warmups executed (warm cache keys, steady throughput).
- 09:00 PT T0: Traffic toggle to 0.1% (slot A).
- 09:10 PT T0+10m: Checkpoint 1 — gate to 0.5% if green.
- 09:30 PT T0+30m: Checkpoint 2 — gate to 1.0% if green.
- 10:00 PT T0+1h: Optional burst to 3% for 15m (only if checklists green).
- 11:20 PT T0+2h20m: Begin extended observation and runbook completion.
- 13:00 PT T0+4h: Complete post-run checklist and write field notes.

Ramp & gating rules (exact thresholds):
- Latency: p99 must not increase > 25% relative to baseline snapshot and absolute p99 < 1200ms.
- Error rate: 5xx increase must be <= 0.05 percentage points and never exceed 0.5% absolute.
- Cost delta: per-token cost estimate should not exceed baseline by > 12% for the route.
- Resource signals: node GPU memory usage must not spike > 10% above baseline in target pool.
- If any gating rule violated during a verification window, immediate rollback to previous route state and initiate forensics.

Smoke & verification tests (automated + manual):
- Automated: run smoke-suite-fastpath.sh which exercises generation, streaming, function-calling, and cache-sensitive prefixes.
- Manual: run product-guided flows (3 reps each) — long-context generation, prefix-primed reranking, and embedding/near-real-time echo tests.
- KV cache validation: verify hit-rate metric increases vs staging baseline and prefix latency drop observed in traces.
- Kernel telemetry: confirm new scheduling heuristic reduces context-switch stalls in hot-path traces.

Rollback criteria & immediate steps:
- Trigger if any hard threshold exceeded in a verification window (latency, errors, GPU OOM, or customer-facing errors).
- Steps:
  1) Toggle traffic back to v2.2 route (immediate route update).
  2) Notify #release-fastpath with reason and basic telemetry snapshot.
  3) Pager call if 15+ min unresolved degradation.
  4) Capture diagnostics: core dump (if OOM), kernel traces, runtime logs, and upload to /tmp/fastpath-artifacts with ticket ENG-5421 linked.
  5) Run post-rollback smoke tests to validate baseline restored.

Post-run checks & artifact capture (T+end):
- [ ] Export final dashboards and mark baseline delta in run diary.
- [ ] Save sampling logs for a 30m window at 1% traffic into artifacts bucket (s3://redwood-release-artifacts/fastpath/2026-05-11/).
- [ ] Run perf diff against staging traces (script: perf-diff.sh).
- [ ] Fill field notes section below with observed anomalies, timestamps, and actions.

Field notes (live capture) — examples of entries to include (fill during run):
- 09:12 PT: saw transient p95 spike to 780ms for 90s; correlated to cache miss storm on node-102. Action: increased cache-rebalancer throttle; spike subsided by 09:16.
- 09:31 PT: kernel scheduler jitter reduced as expected; p99 improved by 8% vs baseline.
- 10:03 PT: brief 502s from a single edge node (edge-7), not customer-impacting; escalated to SRE. No rollback.

Release notes draft (to include with outward-facing release when experiment graduates):
- Feature highlights:
  - FastPath scheduling heuristic enabled for a small production cohort: reduces tail latency on short-context generations by ~8% in initial tests.
  - KV-cache priming strategy added: warms hot prefixes proactively to reduce cold-start latency.
- Bug fixes:
  - Fix for rare kernel-level context-switch hang under heavy prefix churn (ENG-5489).
- Known issues and caveats:
  - Mini-roll only in us-west-2; some latency improvements not observed on long-tail, low-frequency prefixes.
  - If customers are pinned to dedicated capacity pools, this routing change will not affect them.
- Migration notes for customers: none required.

Open items & questions (to resolve post-run):
- Revisit alert thresholds for p95 vs p99 in large-scale runs (is 25% p99 cap appropriate?).
- Tuning cache rebalancer default throttle for multi-tenant noise.
- Decide on expanded roll to regional control-plane next quarter (proposal PR pending).

Attachments & quick links (for run lead):
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
- Linked Jira tickets: ENG-5421 (fastpath rollout), ENG-5489 (kernel hang fix), ENG-5510 (perf regression investigation)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/FASTPATH-2026
- Post-run artifact location: s3://redwood-release-artifacts/fastpath/2026-05-11/

Notes on uniqueness of this run:
This mini-roll aims to combine a scheduling heuristic change (low-level runtime improvement) with a higher-level KV-cache priming strategy — the combination exposes interactions between kernel scheduling and cache eviction policies. Because interactions are subtle and potentially transient, the experiment uses very short verification windows and conservatively tight gating. Field notes are intentionally prescriptive so follow-ups can be targeted (SRE playbooks, kernel tweaks, cache policy adjustments).

Run-lead signoff:
- Run lead: Priya Nair — signature: pnair (slack)
- SRE approval: Marta Silva — signature: marta-sre
- Runtime owner: Ethan Brooks — signature: ebrooks

(End of draft)
